questions.question: Q: Name the three main stages of the choreographic process.

points.text: Exploration, selection and refinement — though the process may revisit stages in any order.

questions.question: Q: Why is exploration an important stage in choreography?

points.text: Exploration allows the choreographer to experiment freely with movement ideas, generating a wide range of material before deciding what works best.

questions.question: Q: How does the choreographic process support GCSE Dance coursework?

points.text: Documenting each stage provides evidence of creative decision-making, which is assessed in the NEA choreography component.

questions.question: Q: Explain why the choreographic process is not always linear.

points.text: Choreographers often revisit earlier stages — for example, refining may reveal the need to explore new ideas or select different material.

questions.question: Q: What is the role of feedback during the choreographic process?

points.text: Feedback from teachers, peers or video review helps the choreographer identify strengths and weaknesses, guiding further refinement.
